title: Ionic Bonding
subject: Chemistry
summary: Move an electron from sodium to chlorine, then join the ions to make sodium chloride.

intro.text: Welcome to Ionic Bonding. You will see how sodium and chlorine join to make sodium chloride.

invalid.text: That move does not work. Read the message to see why, then try again.

missions.title: Move an electron
missions.goalText: Give sodium's outer electron to chlorine, so both end with a complete outer shell (an octet).
hints: Look at the outer shells. Sodium has 1 outer electron. Chlorine has 7.
Sodium is the metal, so it gives. Chlorine is the non-metal, so it takes.
Drag sodium's outer electron onto chlorine, or tap sodium and then tap chlorine. Then press Check.

start.text: Sodium has 1 electron in its outer shell. Chlorine has 7. Move sodium's outer electron to chlorine.

complete.text: Well done. Sodium lost one electron and became Na+. Chlorine gained it and became Cl-. Both now have a complete outer shell, an octet.

questions.prompt: Sodium (2,8,1) gives one electron to chlorine. What does sodium become?
questions.explanation: Sodium loses its one outer electron, so it has 11 protons and 10 electrons. That is a charge of +1, and the electrons fill 2,8, a complete outer shell (an octet).

questions.prompt: Why does chlorine take an electron instead of giving its electrons away?

options.label: It has 1 outer electron, which is easy to lose
It has 7 outer electrons, so gaining 1 completes its octet
It has no outer electrons at all
Its outer shell is already complete

questions.explanation: Chlorine is 2,8,7. Gaining one electron gives 2,8,8, a complete outer shell (an octet). Losing seven electrons would take much more.

missions.title: Join the ions
missions.goalText: Join Na+ and Cl- to make sodium chloride, NaCl.
hints: Na+ is positive and Cl- is negative. Opposite charges attract.
Both ions already have a complete outer shell, so they are ready to join.
Press Join the ions, then press Check.

start.text: Na+ and Cl- have opposite charges, so they attract each other. Join the ions to make sodium chloride.

complete.text: This attraction between oppositely charged ions is an ionic bond. You made sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.prompt: What holds Na+ and Cl- together in sodium chloride?

options.label: A pair of electrons shared between them
The nucleus of one atom moving into the other
Nothing; the ions only sit next to each other

questions.explanation: Na+ is positive and Cl- is negative. Opposite charges attract. This attraction between ions is an ionic bond. Sharing electrons is a different kind of bond.

questions.prompt: What is the total charge of one unit of sodium chloride, NaCl?
questions.explanation: The +1 charge of Na+ and the -1 charge of Cl- cancel out, so NaCl has no overall charge. The electron moved from sodium to chlorine; none were made or lost.
